compare.label: Compare r2 with Choose a revision…r1 · candidate
items: Changed: The takeaway r1: Each request spends one token from its user's bucket; tokens drip back slowly, so a user who asks faster than the drip empties the bucket and the next request is rejected. Every bucket lives centrally, in Redis. r2: Each request spends one token from its user's bucket; a burst empties it, the next request is refused, and the bucket refills at a steady rate. Every user's bucket lives centrally, in Redis.

Changed: The demonstration r1: One user's bucket holds three tokens. Request 1 is admitted and spends a token; one token drips back. Requests 2–4 arrive faster than the drip and spend all three. Request 5 finds the bucket empty and is rejected with 429. A token then drips back in. The bucket is revealed as one of many per-user buckets in Redis. r2: One user's bucket holds 3 tokens. Request A takes one. A burst of B, C and D arrives before any refill lands: B and C take the last two and D is refused with a 429. During a held beat, two drops refill the bucket. Request E is admitted, and one more drop lands as the view pulls back to Redis. The refill is shown as N tokens per second, the same N as the request rate limiter's cap.
Changed: The counted example r1: tokens in this user's bucket: 3 → 1 over 7 changes r2: tokens in this user's bucket: 3 → 2 over 8 changes
Changed: Moment "Under the hood" renamed r1: Under the hood r2: Open the limiter

Changed: One request, one token: what the viewer sees r1: Bucket full (3) → request 1 arrives from the user, one token lifts out, lit in the accent, and rides with the request out towards the API → bucket holds 2, its level drops one step r2: 3 tokens → 2; request A passes through to the API carrying its token

Changed: A burst drains it: what the viewer sees r1: Bucket at 2 → the inlet swells slowly, a drop falls and settles as a token → bucket at 3, level back up r2: 2 tokens → 0; the level empties while the inlet drop swells but does not fall

Changed: Refused: what the viewer sees r1: Bucket at 3 → requests 2, 3 and 4 arrive in quick succession, each taking one token → bucket at 0, level at the floor, the inlet's next drop still only half formed r2: D approaches → stops at the empty rim → recoils back along its route with a 429; the bucket stays at 0
Changed: Moment "Rejected — then a token returns" renamed r1: Rejected — then a token returns r2: Hold on the refill

Changed: Hold on the refill: what the viewer sees r1: Bucket at 0 → request 5 arrives, takes nothing, recoils back along the lane lit in the accent with a 429 tag → after the line, a drop falls and the bucket holds 1 r2: 0 tokens → 2 in two equal steps; the level rises with each landing

Changed: Name the rate: what the viewer sees r1: One bucket filling the frame → the same bucket, with its one token, sitting among other users' buckets inside a Redis store panel r2: 2 tokens → 1; request E passes to the API

Added: Every bucket, in Redis r2: The view pulls back once. Our bucket shrinks into one slot in a row of buckets inside a Redis store panel; each of the other buckets holds its own count. One more drop lands in ours as the view settles.
